title: Robusta roaster in Ho Chi Minh City
subtitle: Coffee roaster selling to cafés, as of 1 Feb 2024
text: I roast robusta in Ho Chi Minh City and sell 1 kg bags to about 60 independent cafés, around 280 bags a week. A bag sells for $8.30 and the green beans plus packaging cost me about $4.90. Beans from the Central Highlands take about 3 weeks to arrive; I keep about 2 weeks of stock and could put about $6,000 into more. My main rival is Highland Supply, who charge $7.90 a bag.

search_terms: robusta coffee price Vietnam Central Highlands

what_happened.text: London robusta futures hit $4,546 a tonne, the peak of the spring run-up; the International Coffee Organization called April's level a 45-year high.
Robusta reached its highest price since 1979 as a drought cut Vietnam's 2023/24 harvest.
Reuters-credited reporting: robusta futures had hit records earlier in the year, mostly after an underwhelming Vietnam harvest and fears over the next one after the drought.
The ICO reported robusta at a 47-year high for two months in a row, averaging 214.7 US cents a pound in July.

caveats: Prices are the example roaster's (the coffee_hcmc example) scaled to early-2024 bean prices. A kilo of roasted coffee needs about 1.19 kg of green beans (a 16% roasting loss), so at 3.33 $/kg that is $3.96 of beans; $0.97 is packaging and other cost. Beans are then 80% of the unit cost, and the price keeps the example's markup. These are a made-up owner's numbers, not a real roaster's.

The price series is the world robusta price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/kg). A Vietnamese roaster pays farm-gate prices in dong, which follow it with a lag and a spread. Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.
Search results are the news before 1 Feb 2024 on robusta and Vietnam's harvest.
